title: Randomized versus quantum query complexity
description: How many input bits must an algorithm read to compute a Boolean function: deterministic, randomized and quantum query complexity. The quantum query model with a proof that measurements can be deferred; amplitude amplification; the adversary bound; Huang's theorem on the sensitivity graph; the inequality D(f) <= C Q(f)^4 for total functions, with complete proofs. Functions with quantum complexity about sqrt(m) and randomized complexity about m^(2-1/k), which show that the exponent 4 is optimal; the randomized lower bound uses one named hypothesis, the Forrelation lower bound of Bansal and Sinha. The course is an exposition of OpenAI's proof (2026).

the minimax theorem for finite games, proved in the course Large independent sets in three-colorable graphs (lesson Alignment of lists: patterns, minimax and Ramsey's theorem)
the lessons prove every other fact they use, except the named hypothesis (BS) of the first lesson, which is used only for the randomized lower bound
